messages.name: John Osborn
messages.subject: Harvard feature idea: a thoughtful gift hiding in the history close to home
messages.text:
Hi John,

I grew up near Harvard and have always loved history, but had never properly explored the Shaker history on our doorstep. Michael surprised me with a day built around it: a little research, a short car trip and time together.

The outing brought back another connection. My mother, Mom-Mom, has always loved Shaker furniture, and growing up we made special trips to stores in Gardner and Lancaster to buy pieces.

I've just shared the memory through An AUsome Life, our independent family publication:
https://anausomelife.com/shaker-history-harvard-family-gift.html

Would this interest the Press as a local feature or a thoughtful, low-cost gift idea for readers? The piece connects a family's furniture memories with Harvard's Shaker heritage and the pleasure of having someone else do the planning. It also includes a fold-open orientation map, links to local history sources and free printable picture cards created for future outings.

I'd be happy to answer questions by email. The outing is a family memory; the map and cards are new companion resources.

Thank you,
An AUsome Life

messages.subject: A family Shaker-history story for Harvard's history community
messages.text:
Hello Harvard Historical Society team,

Your Shaker Village history is linked in a new family story we've published at An AUsome Life, and I wanted to share it with you.

Michael surprised me with a Shaker history day around Harvard. I grew up nearby and love history, yet had never taken the time to explore these places. It also brought back memories of my mother, Mom-Mom, and our special trips to furniture stores in Gardner and Lancaster to buy Shaker furniture.

The story is about a thoughtful gift that takes research and time together, without needing a large budget:
https://anausomelife.com/shaker-history-harvard-family-gift.html

Would you consider sharing the link in a Society newsletter or on your social page? It offers readers a personal way into the area's history, alongside links to local sources, an original chair watercolor and a fold-open orientation map. We also created printable picture cards for future history outings.

Suggested sharing caption: A little research, a short drive and a thoughtful surprise: An AUsome Life explores Harvard's Shaker history and family memories of Shaker furniture.

Please credit An AUsome Life / @anausomelife and link to the story. Thank you for helping people discover the history close to home.

Warmly,
An AUsome Life
